titulo.en: Just in case, to top it all

intro.en: Por and para at B2: the contrasts that change the meaning, and the fixed phrases.

por poco.nota: Por poco me caigo: I nearly fell. Spanish uses the present.

no es para tanto.en: it's not such a big deal

texto.en:
**Por** looks at what lies behind: the cause (por amor), the doer (escrito **por**), the exchange (lo compré **por** diez euros), on someone's behalf (hazlo **por** mí), the way through (**por** el parque), rough time and place (**por** la mañana, **por** aquí), the means (**por** correo), the rate (dos veces **por** semana), and what is still to do (queda mucho **por** hacer).

**Para** looks ahead: the purpose, the receiver, the direction (salgo **para** Madrid), the deadline (**para** el lunes), an opinion (**para mí**), an employer (trabajo **para** un banco), and a comparison with what you would expect: **para ser** extranjero, habla muy bien.

Minimal pairs: lo hice **por ti** (because of you) and lo hice **para ti** (to give to you). **Por mí**, vale (I don't mind) and **para mí**, es un error (in my view).

**Estar para** is to be about to, or in the mood for: no estoy **para** bromas. **Estar por** is to be inclined to, or still to be done.

filas: Lo hice por ti. (because of you)
Lo hice para ti. (to give to you)
Para mí, es un error. (in my view)

frases.es: ¡Por fin llegas! Por poco pierdo el tren.
frases.en: You're here at last! I nearly missed the train.

frases.es: Perdona. Había un atasco y, para colmo, me quedé sin gasolina.
frases.en: Sorry. There was a traffic jam and, to top it all, I ran out of petrol.

frases.es: Bueno, no es para tanto. ¿Llevas paraguas?
frases.en: Well, it's not such a big deal. Have you got an umbrella?

frases.es: Sí, por si acaso. Por lo visto, va a llover.
frases.en: Yes, just in case. Apparently it's going to rain.

frases.es: Para ser tan despistado, hoy vienes muy preparado.
frases.en: For someone so absent-minded, you've come very well prepared today.
As far as I'm concerned, we can go now.

pregunta.en: Complete: I did it for your sake, because of you.

por.en: The motive behind the action: por.

para.en: Para ti would mean it was meant for you to have.

de.en: De ti would mean about you or from you.

pregunta.en: Complete: for a foreigner, he speaks very well.

Para.en: A comparison with what you would expect: para.

Por.en: Por ser extranjero would mean because he is a foreigner.

De.en: De does not make this comparison.

pregunta.en: Complete: there is a lot still to do.

por.en: Por plus infinitive: still to be done.

para.en: Para hacer would give a purpose.

a.en: A hacer is not used here.

explicacion.en: Por poco means nearly, and the present refers to the past.

texto.en: I fell for a short time.

pregunta.en: A friend suggests a film. You do not mind either way. What do you say?

Por mí, vale.en: As far as I'm concerned, fine.

Para mí, vale.en: Para mí gives an opinion or names the receiver.

Por ti, vale.en: That would mean for your sake.

bloques.frase: Para colmo, me quedé sin gasolina

traduccion.en: To top it all, I ran out of petrol.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the story of a terrible day, with por, para and at least five set phrases: por fin, por lo visto, para colmo, por si acaso…

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud what precautions you take before a trip, and why.
